pages.text: The controller screen shows core temperature, state, heat, power, efficiency, radiators, rods and $(danger)time to core failure$().

pages.title: Rods
pages.text: Load up to $(bold)4 fuel rods$(). Each makes $(bold)35 kW$() of heat at full insertion.$(br2)Rod slots lock above 350°C.

pages.title: Insertion
pages.text: The slider sets rod insertion. $(bold)Follow$() matches network demand plus 5 kW to charge batteries, minus other generators, capped at what the radiators can shed.

pages.title: Reserve
pages.text: The $(bold)Res$() button holds 0, 10, 20, 40 or 60 kW above demand, so a sudden load is already covered.$(br2)Unused heat leaves through the radiators. $(danger)Rods burn faster.$()

pages.title: Cold Start
pages.text: $(danger)Below 0°C for a day, the coolant freezes$(): no fission, no radiators.$(br2)Keep the room at 5°C or warmer for 3 minutes to thaw it. A cold core warms at full insertion first.

pages.title: Idle
pages.text: Pumps stop when the core is idle and below 40°C, so it settles to room temperature.$(br2)The casing leaks a little heat into the room.

pages.title: Redstone
pages.text: A redstone signal trips SCRAM. A comparator reads core temperature.
